fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` carries `timeout_func_only = true` (added by story
`bold-abeyant-indri`, commit `6a5c88027c5`, at `pyproject.toml:664`). pytest-timeout documents
that key as deferring the timeout evaluation to only the test function body, ignoring fixture
time — so fixture SETUP and TEARDOWN are unguarded by the per-test hang budget. That is the
exact phase the guard was originally built for: bug `89d5-61da-b621-47f8` was filed because a
`with TestClient(app)` teardown awaited `queue.join()` under a 1200 s drain and burned the full
60-minute job cap. The guard that landed then (`--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, no
`func_only`) covered all phases; the current ini does not.

## Approach

Drop the `timeout_func_only = true` line from `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` so the key reverts to
pytest-timeout's upstream default (`False`) and the 300 s budget covers fixture setup and
teardown again. This is the ecosystem-standard shape: pytest-timeout's own default for
`func_only` is `False` and its README positions `func_only` as a last-resort workaround
("firstly make the timeouts larger"); pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn configure no
`timeout_func_only`. The 300 s budget is already sized to DWARF the slowest legitimate test
(measured worst `call` 29.93 s, pinned in `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py`), so
charging fixture time to the first requesting test carries low trip risk. Default: if CI shows
any slow-fixture test tripping the budget after this lands, RAISE that test's own timeout with
`@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` (the README-sanctioned remedy) rather than restoring `func_only`.
Not `session_timeout`: it is cooperative — evaluated between tests — so it cannot stop a
hanging test. The rewritten ini comment cites this ticket and `89d5-61da-b621-47f8`.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml` — remove `timeout_func_only = true`; rewrite the budget comment block to
  explain full-phase coverage, citing `797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5` and `89d5-61da-b621-47f8`.
- `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` — update the config assertion
  (`test_the_configured_budget_is_the_measured_one`) to require the key's ABSENCE; add the two
  out-of-process arms described under Testing. Rework the EXISTING material for coherence with
  the new policy: the module docstring (currently framing the positive arm around
  `func_only=True`) is rewritten to describe full-phase coverage and the plain-marker remedy;
  the existing positive arm `test_a_marked_test_may_outrun_the_ini_budget` keeps its purpose
  (marker beats ini) but its generated project drops `timeout_func_only = true` and its
  generated marker becomes `@pytest.mark.timeout(120)` (no `func_only`); the existing negative
  arm's generated ini likewise drops the key; the in-repo `@pytest.mark.timeout(180,
  func_only=True)` guards on the arm functions themselves become `@pytest.mark.timeout(180)`.
- `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` — comment-only: reword the sentence that
  explains the measured worst times in terms of `timeout_func_only = true`.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md` — update the per-test hang budget section (it currently documents
  `timeout_func_only = true` and the body-only semantics), including its example override
  snippet, which shows `@pytest.mark.timeout(90, func_only=True)`.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — comment-only: the default-suite step's comment
  (lines 660–662) prescribes `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` for legitimately
  longer tests; reword it to the plain `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` remedy so it does not
  contradict the new full-phase policy. No `run:` command changes.

## Testing

Both new arms run out-of-process against a generated project via the shared
`run_nested_pytest` helper (the same style as the existing negative arm in
`tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py`, per story 25b4's single-launch-site guard), each with a
deliberately tiny budget so they cost seconds:

- Negative arm (hang coverage): a generated project mirrors this repo's ini keys (timeout=2,
  `timeout_method = "thread"`, no `func_only`) and contains a test whose FIXTURE SETUP sleeps
  past the budget, and a second project whose TEARDOWN sleeps past it; both nested runs must
  fail with a pytest-timeout `Timeout` naming the test, not hang.
- Positive arm (the sanctioned remedy): in a generated project with `timeout = 2` and a shared
  fixture that sleeps past that budget, a test carrying `@pytest.mark.timeout(30)` passes —
  proving a legitimately slow-fixture test has a supported per-test escape, so dropping
  `func_only` does not force fixture cost onto an unraisable budget.

`make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the targeted suites
(`pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py`) run
green before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` no longer sets `timeout_func_only`; checked by the updated
      config assertion in `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` failing if the key reappears.
- [x] A test whose SETUP or TEARDOWN hangs is bounded and names itself rather than running to
      the job cap; demonstrated by the out-of-process nested-pytest negative arms (fixture-
      setup hang and teardown hang) asserting a `Timeout` failure in the nested run.
- [x] A legitimately slow shared fixture does not strand its test without recourse: the
      positive arm proves `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` on the test covers fixture time and passes
      under a tighter ini budget.
- [x] The chosen configuration is recorded in `pyproject.toml` with a comment citing this
      ticket (`797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5`) and `89d5-61da-b621-47f8`; checked by reading the ini
      comment block in the landed change.
